text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Director of the Oslo Bourse, Lars Froensdal, wants to privatise the stock exchange. Foreign investors account for about 50 percent of current turnover. Froensdal fears the bourse will become sidelined as Norwegian companies become listed on other exchanges, which will increasingly compete with the Oslo market.
- A survey of 1,300 Norwegian business managers commissioned by employment agency, Vikarbyraa, revealed that 39 percent of managers consider it difficult to find qualified employees.

- Insurance companies have so far received 600 claims for damage caused by heavy stroms across the country at the weekend. Power was cut off at more than 25,000 households during the storms and many buildings suffered roof damage. In Tromsoe more than 100 trees were blown down.

- Aker RGI may take over pharmaceutical group Nycomed ASA. Head of Aker RGI, Bjoern Rune Gjelsten, said on Thursday the group's next billon-crown investment may come soon, but he declined to say when it might be.

- NatWest Securities is recommending shares in shipping company Stolt-Nielsen at 102 crowns. Poor results for Stolt Comex Seaways and low spot rates for chemical tankers are expected to have a negative impact on the share price in the short term. However, the broker firm believes the negative trend soon will turn.
